caption: A wind-up alarm clock rings, and its little hammer hammers between the two bells and the clock shivers on the table.

sa.check: A wind-up alarm clock with two bells on top stands on a table.
The little hammer swings between the bells.
The clock shivers on the table.
The hammer moves rapidly back and forth.
The hammer swings and the clock shivers at the same time.

pc.expect: The hammer swings from its base between the two bells and the clock trembles in place.
pc.fail: The clock shivers while the hammer hangs still; or the clock glides smoothly across the table; or the hammer detaches and floats; or the bells swing on their own while the hammer is still.

pc.expect: While the hammer swings the clock shivers; when the hammer stops the clock stands still.
pc.fail: The hammer swings hard and the clock stands dead still; or the hammer stops and the clock keeps shivering unchanged; or the hammer swings but stays clear of both bells for the whole clip.

pc.expect: The clock stays on the table; if it walks to the edge it falls.
pc.fail: The clock lifts off the table; or tips and hangs at an angle unsupported; or rises up on end.

pc.expect: The clock case and bells are rigid; the hammer is a rigid head on a thin stalk.
pc.fail: The bells dent or wobble like rubber; or the clock case bends; or the hammer stalk stretches.

pc.expect: One clock with two bells and one hammer; the hammer does not pass through a bell.
pc.fail: A third bell appears; or the hammer vanishes; or the hammer passes through a bell; or the clock duplicates.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The clock face, its hands and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The clock face changes; or the hands jump; or the table changes.
